data.name: Reinald
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Germanic elements ‘Rain’ meaning advice and ‘Wald’ meaning rule. This name was given to those who were advisers or rulers. In Christian tradition, this name is associated with the Holy Roman Emperor and Saint Reinald of Brussels.

in_latin.name: Reinaldus
in_latin.meaning: Nomen alemannicum significans virtutem et fortitudinem
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Reinaldus alemannicum est, quod virtutem et fortitudinem significat. Originem trahit a regno Alemannorum, ubi erat notus pro suo valore militari. In medio aevum, nomen huius generis apparuit in multis locis Europae, et erat communiter attributum hominibus qui virtutem et fortitudinem habebant. In Christianismo, nomen Reinaldus significat potentiam Dei et fortitudinem fidei.

in_english.name: Reinald
in_english.meaning: Germanic name meaning strength and courage
in_english.long_meaning: The name Reinald is of Germanic origin, meaning strength and courage. It is derived from the Old High German words 'rein' meaning 'pure' and 'wald' meaning 'power, strength'. In the Middle Ages, the name Reinaldus appeared in various European locations, and was commonly attributed to men who possessed strength and courage. In Christianity, the name Reinald signifies the power of God and the strength of faith.

data.spiritual_significance: Saint Reinald of Brussels is the primary spiritual figure associated with this name. Born in the late 11th or early 12th Century, he was the second Bishop of Liège and counts as one of the greatest saints of the Archdiocese of Mechelen-Brussels. Known for his extraordinary asceticism, meditative nature, and healing abilities, Saint Reinald became a revered Christian figure. Individuals bearing this name may find inspiration from his spirituality and stoicism, alongside the sense of guidance and protection that the patriarchal significance of the name offers.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Reinald was a Frankish king who ruled in the 5th century. The name Reinald carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.
